name: Module 1: Identifying the Customer - Discovery Call
description: Practice qualifying a suspect through payment processing discovery. A restaurant owner was referred to you but has done no research on Payroc. Prove you can identify the customer through proper discovery and qualification.

conversation_config.conversational_context: This is a training simulation call. The caller is a new Payroc sales rep practicing discovery and qualification for payment processing services. The call should last approximately 10 minutes. Do not break character.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Hi — hello? Oh hey, sorry, I was just wrapping up something. So you're the person Dave mentioned, right? He said someone from — what was it — might reach out. I've got a few minutes before the dinner rush. What can I help you with?

behaviors.description: Asked open-ended questions BEFORE presenting solutions
Asked about current pain points or frustrations
Asked about current payment processing situation
Asked about specific needs or problems to solve
Asked follow-up questions to quantify or deepen pain points
Kept conversation focused on payment processing, not POS
Asked about budget, current fees, or financial impact
Asked why this is a priority right now
Asked about timeline, urgency, or contract dates
Treated prospect as a suspect, did not assume ready to buy
Did not push product features before understanding needs
Identified engagement signals before advancing the conversation
Earned the right to propose a next step appointment
Did not push for a sale or close on the first call
Set clear expectations for follow-up timing and format

key_concepts: Suspect = fits ICP but no proven interest
Prospect = qualified with confirmed need, budget, authority, timeline
Customer-focused reps ask before they tell
CHAMP leads with challenges, usually gets better engagement
This module focuses on PAYMENT PROCESSING, not POS
common_mistakes: Feature-dumping before asking about the prospect's situation
Treating a suspect like a prospect from minute one
Pushing for a close instead of a follow-up
Skipping stages, trying to close before discovering pain
